## 2. Weekend gaps and buffers

Upward gaps only (a stock-loan market loses when the borrowed stock gets dearer). *Empirical* = 10y Fri close → Mon open (65.5h, 3-day weekends 89.5h: conservative vs the 48h/72h 24/5 freeze). *FHS* = filtered historical simulation: each gap standardized by the trailing σ that Friday, bootstrapped and rescaled to the launch σ. The 99.9% gap used below is the larger of the two.

| Stock | Weekends | σ 1y / 3y / 5y / 10y | b 48h / 72h (z 2.5) | Max up gap 10y | Empirical 99.9% up | FHS 99.9% up | 99.9% used | Gap that leaves a max-LTV position underwater |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SPY | 511 (14% 3-day) | 13.0% / 15.2% / 17.2% / 18.0% | 3.1% / 3.9% | 3.9% | 3.9% | 2.6% | 3.9% | 24.7% |
| AAPL | 511 (14% 3-day) | 24.6% / 26.7% / 28.0% / 29.1% | 5.2% / 6.3% | 6.7% | 6.6% | 5.9% | 6.6% | 27.2% |
| NVDA | 511 (14% 3-day) | 37.6% / 46.7% / 51.6% / 49.8% | 9.6% / 11.8% | 7.5% | 6.6% | 6.9% | 6.9% | 32.5% |

**Reading.** NVDA: the 99.9% upward gap is at or below the 48h buffer, so at the 99.9% level no position at the worst allowed LTV even becomes liquidatable, whatever the cap. SPY, AAPL: the 99.9% gap exceeds the buffer by 0.8% (SPY), 1.4% (AAPL), so max-LTV positions become liquidatable and the cap must fit the liquidation in the DEX band (§3). For every stock the gap that leaves a max-LTV position underwater (bad debt even with perfect liquidity) is at least 4× the largest upward weekend gap in 10 years, so LLTV 77% and z 2.5 hold; the gaps above the buffer are liquidity questions, not LLTV questions.

## 3. Caps against measured DEX depth

Depth = USD that moves the pools (USDG + WETH, summed) 2% up, i.e. what a liquidator can buy within 2% slippage (< LIF − 1 = 7.41%). The minimum over all snapshots is used; liquidity beyond the 2% band is ignored.

| Stock | 2% push-up depth: weekend min / weekday | Min used | Cap for $0 bad debt at 99.9% | Stress cap: all debt liquidatable just above the buffer | P(bad debt) per weekend at launch cap (25%) | at D8 target | Per-address cap: launch → 25% of depth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SPY | $302,459 / $325,334 | $302,459 (weekend 2026-09-27T19:08) | $323,403 | $325,815 | 0.000% | 0.000% | $75,000 → $75,615 +1% |
| AAPL | $140,972 / $144,449 | $140,972 (weekend 2026-09-27T19:08) | $147,002 | $148,919 | 0.000% | 0.409% | $35,000 → $35,243 +1% |
| NVDA | $1,054,025 / $665,543 | $665,543 (weekday 2026-09-28T17:02) | ∞ | $674,577 | 0.000% | 0.000% | $250,000 → $166,386 **-33% ⚑** |

**Weekday vs weekend depth (flag).** NVDA's weekday 2% push-up depth ($665,543, both pools) is -37% vs the lowest weekend snapshot ($1,054,025); SPY and AAPL are within ±25%. The D8 per-address rule (25% of 2% depth) would give NVDA $166,386 instead of $250k. **Not changed** (owner rule: flag before touching caps). One weekday snapshot is one point; rerun on two more weekday sessions before deciding.

**Reading.** The launch caps (25% of D8) are at or below both the 99.9% cap and the stress cap for SPY, AAPL, NVDA: at launch every position could be liquidated at once inside the 2% band. At the full D8 targets: SPY $1,000,000 vs sim $323,403 **-68% ⚑**; AAPL $250,000 vs sim $147,002 **-41% ⚑**; NVDA $1,000,000 vs sim ∞ not binding. **The D8 targets are not changed here**: they only apply after the ×2 steps (10: 2 clean weekends and a sim rerun each), and the rerun at each step uses the depth measured then. P(bad debt) is the share of simulated weekends whose gap exceeds the buffer *and* whose liquidatable notional exceeds the band (or the gap exceeds the underwater gap); it is 0 in the FHS for SPY because no standardized draw exceeds the buffer at σ 17%, while the 10y empirical maximum (+3.9%, 2020-11-09) does — hence the 99.9% cap uses the larger of the two.

## 6. Limits of this model

- Worst-case book: every position at the maximum LTV and the vault at U_MAX. Real books are spread out, so actual liquidation volume is lower.
- Depth outside the 2% band is ignored and pools are not refilled by arbitrage during the liquidation (conservative); depth is a handful of snapshots, not a time series.
- The 10y gaps are for 65.5h/89.5h closures of a regular-hours market; the 24/5 feed freezes for ~48h and tracks Friday evening and Sunday night trading.
- The FHS assumes standardized gaps are stationary; regime changes (a crash weekend) are only as likely as in 2016–2026.
- Earnings gaps use Yahoo dates and the after-close session for all 10y NVDA/AAPL prints (every date in the window is AMC).
